Synopsis:
The US is escalating sanctions on Iran's oil exports, targeting Chinese "teapot" refiners and shipping intermediaries that have sustained Iranian crude flows to China. Chinese imports of Iranian oil have fallen sharply — from ~1.57m bbl/day in February to ~534k bbl/day in August — driven by the US naval blockade of Iran's ports reinstated in July. Washington is threading a needle: pressuring China without triggering retaliation on critical minerals or derailing Trump-Xi talks. Beijing rejects unilateral sanctions and signals it will protect its interests. The situation remains fluid, with sanctions enforcement intensifying but diplomatic constraints limiting their full scope.
